svg.title: QP2609 Q4 - D5: Fuel in use, cylinder-oil BN, feed-rate mode and condition monitoring (Everllence B&W)
svg.desc: Decision flow with a monitoring return path. The fuel in use decides the oil: high-sulphur fuel above 0.50 percent sulphur takes a Cat. II BN 100 to 140+ oil or an ACOM mix, and the feed rate is the feed-rate factor times sulphur percent, never below the minimum. Fuel of 0 to 0.50 percent sulphur and LNG, ethane, LPG or methanol take a Cat. II BN 40 oil and the feed rate is governed by the minimum feed-rate setting. Monitoring - daily consumption, scavenge drain oil analysis, monthly port inspection and wear measurement - decides whether to reduce in small steps, hold, or restore and raise the feed or the BN; the result returns to the feed setting and monitoring starts again.
svg.text: Q4 - D5 Fuel in use -> oil BN -> feed-rate mode -> monitoring (Everllence B&W Mk 9+ and dual-fuel)
BN and feed rate are SEPARATE decisions. Maker guidance for this engine family only - do not transfer to another maker. No feed-rate figures shown.
Fuel in use
sulphur % from the bunker delivery note, entered on
the MOP (DF: pilot-fuel sulphur)
HSFO, above 0.50% S
(e.g. ships with exhaust gas scrubbers)
Oil: Cat. II BN 100-140+
or an ACOM mix with a lower-BN oil
Feed: feed-rate factor x S%
(FRF, formerly the ACC factor), load-dependent,
never below the minimum feed rate; FRF
lowered only on sweep-test / drain-oil
evidence; if FRF must be high, raise BN
0-0.50% S fuel, LNG, ethane,
LPG or methanol
Oil: Cat. II BN 40
same oil for gas/methanol as for VLSFO/ULSFO
Feed: the MINIMUM feed-rate setting
(FRF x S% falls below the minimum, so the
factor is not relevant); optimise by
inspection, never below the maker minimum
Changeover
HSFO <-> low-S fuel: change
the oil (ACOS2 switch or
ACOM BN) AND the S% entry.
Within 0-0.50% S and gas:
same oil; update the S% entry
Ammonia (ME-LGIA)
no ammonia-specific guidance
found - follow engine documents
Load control (all cases): feed proportional to load above the part-load breakpoint, to engine speed below it; raised temporarily during load changes (LCD)
Condition monitoring - repeated after every change (return path below)
daily: measured cylinder-oil consumption against the MOP calculated figure (a shortfall is a fault - raise the feed and investigate)
scavenge drain oil: residual BN and total / magnetic iron - accredited laboratory as the reference, onboard kits as a supplement
monthly scavenge-port inspection of liners, rings and deposits (more often while reducing); wear measurement at overhaul
Good condition, acceptable iron
reduce in small steps, hold and re-check;
never below the maker minimum
Raised iron, deposits, micro-seizure, scuffing
restore the previous good setting or raise the feed;
on HSFO with persistent corrosion, raise the BN
Return path: the outcome sets the next feed (or BN) setting - then monitor again.
Sources: MAN SL2023-737 (June 2023) sections 1-7 and App. I; Everllence SL2025-776 (Nov 2025); Everllence project guide G95ME-C10.5-GI, 7020-0260-14ppr rev 1.0 (July 2026), 9.01-9.02.
